data.gender_notes: Navi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Navratri is a nine-day festival dedicated to nine forms of Shakti, or divine feminine energy. Navi means 'new' or 'fresh'. It is a name for a newborn, symbolizing the fresh start of a new life. The name Navi carries the meaning “New, Fresh” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Navi usually hope their child will grow to embody new, fresh and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Navi represents the new beginning of life, filled with hope and positivity. It signifies the journey towards spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Navi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “New, Fresh.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Navi total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Navi Dweepa or Nava Dweepa, also known as the 'Seven Islands of Hindustan', refers to a sacred geographical location in Hinduism, which is believed to consist of seven major islands. These islands are considered sacred as they are believed to be the abodes of various Hindu gods and goddesses. The concept of Navi Dweepa is mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Skanda Purana and the Mahabharata. The exact time period for this belief is unclear but it is believed to have originated in ancient India.

Navaratri, also known as Navratri or Durga Puja, is a major Hindu festival celebrated in India and Nepal. Navaratri means 'nine nights' in Sanskrit. The festival is dedicated to the worship of nine forms of Goddess Shakti or Durga. Each night of the festival is dedicated to a specific form of the goddess, and the ninth day is celebrated as Vijayadashami or Dussehra. Navi is a form of Goddess Durga and is worshipped on the seventh day of Navaratri, known as Saptami or Sharad Navratri. The exact time period for Navaratri varies each year but it usually falls in the months of September or October.
